reviews.review: Great fun, and always getting better...also, free.

Warframe brings forth a new light over the co-op TPS concept. Not only does it allow for dynamic, compelling and visually advanced PVE / PVP gameplay but also there is a very well developped customization and upgrade system which, once it has been fully mastered (average learning curve of an hour following the recent rebuild of it i would say) puts players in a position where possibilities appear to be numerous if not limitless. The only flaw one should maybe point out is the lack of story-telling and background, yet  and since the game still is in an open beta testing phase this could be taken care of within the next few months or so. Digital Extreme's follow-up to 2007's Dark Sector has a lot to offer and there supposedly is a lot more to come.
Only the bravest of tennos will see the bright light of a new day shine upon the scorched galaxy!
Great game with constant universe and content expansion, everything is accessible through simply playing, and space ninjas...

Originally recommended this game, now I don't. Here's why:

// Intro //
 
I started playing this game in 2013-ish back when it was still almost literally ninjas in space. So I've been on the ride up until this point where I have decided to quit the game several times due to several design choices that I think are more time consuming than fun; as well as other design choices that basically turn this game into a completely different game that I'm not a fan of anymore.

The core gameplay of the game is still fun. The idea is you progress your Warframes, weapons, sentinels - now pets, ships, mechs (which is going down a road I don't like but we'll get to that) - on various mission types that give you a sense of the world that has been built. You get a sense of power progression as your levels go up, you unlock more ways to obtain power, be it through new weapons, sentinels, mods, etc. 

There wasn't a real story for a long time, but even the "story" they've added just makes no sense to me - I think the writing gets away with being very amateur just because of how ambiguous it is, which I think will only work to a point.

// Positives //

As I pointed out, the core game is fun. It's packed with parkour animations, fun run-and-gun gameplay along with decent melee combat. Visuals are very flashy with the sound effects to reinforce it. The art and sound teams did a great job.

Group gameplay feels very rewarding. You don't have to fight over any loot, which encourages more group play in my opinion.

Having a sentinel or pet with you adds another layer to your gameplay. Your companion can be modded to protect you, go full on damage mode, or both if you build correctly.

Mission variety exceeds most standards I think. Some missions are objectively not fun, but overall there is plenty to do and it's fun content. Usually.

// Negatives //

One of the first things that was added to the game that made me start disliking it was the addition of the operator. This added yet another layer of things to keep up with because your operator is not just an aesthetic addition - it's part of the gameplay and in some cases necessary in order to progress in the game. But I dealt with it.

The other things that started to bother me was the addition of so many Warframes that not only started to imbalance the game, but also moved away from the whole "space ninjas" thing. There are hardly any new Warframes that have a subtle yet interesting design. The main one that I liked at first but then ended up making me dislike it was the Nidus Phryke skin. The design looks neat especially in concept art, but it's so... "big". They did this again but took it to another level with the Zephyr Harrier skin - I don't even know what to say about that one honestly. It just doesn't match the game whatsoever.

With every "open world" they add to the game, they also add additional resources you have to grind for in order to get some of the new gear they release with that update. Ever since I got my first Cetus crafted weapon, I just ignored the system entirely. It's such a long grind to get parts to begin with, and even more so for the resources to get Arcanes. This grind isn't fun because the number of things I need is so high - even if I'm in a fun mission, the number of things I know I need are still in my head and I think about the amount of times I'm going to have to do the mission in order to unlock something. It's dumb and doesn't respect my time.

They've also added mechs called Necramechs. I got so frustrated with the grind to make one that I just used platinum to buy one. Why did I do this? Because not only do Necramechs make certain missions easier, they are a necessity in some Railjack missions - another thing that was frustrating for me to get. I wanted to do Railjack missions since I spent so long getting the damned thing, but then I get to a mission where another player ends up telling me that a Necramech is required to do a certain part - something I didn't have at the time.

// Conclusion //

Just so I can stop complaining, I'll sum everything up.

The game is going in a totally different and weird direction than where I think it should go. It doesn't respect my time, especially because the rewards do not reflect the time spent. The developers historically don't take critique very well, especially when they feel more emotionally attached to a certain part of the game - so that makes this whole thing worse.

It seems like whoever is making the decisions at the studio has a huge vision but doesn't realize it does not fit within the scope of Warframe. It's like they're jamming square pegs into a triangular hole constantly and telling players "It's ok! We'll fix it!" and they hardly ever do.
